title: Ambient Occlusion bake appears too dark with thick export
content:
Does anyone experience an issue when exporting from Marvelous Designer to Substance Painter using the **Thick** option, where the Ambient Occlusion bake appears too dark or black around areas like attached pockets or additional fabric layers? How can this be fixed?![397d015345a6476699b29fba481c3b9d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/7e701247ab4d49f5b6cf3247fc8f275a/images/397d015345a6476699b29fba481c3b9dimage_2025-06-09_171540189.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I asked ChatGPT and it replied:When exporting with "Thick" option:MD creates two-sided geometry (inner and outer surface), resulting in very tight gaps between fabric layers.These narrow spaces cause ray occlusion artifacts during AO baking — rays bounce between the tight layers, resulting in overly dark shadows.In overlapping parts like pockets, this is amplified because the geometry is even closer.
Reply 1: ✅ Solutions and Workarounds: 1. Use "Thin" Export and Add Thickness in Painter or Later Best Practice: Export with the "Thin" option from MD, and add thickness as a normal map or displacement in Painter or during rendering.Why? This avoids problematic geometry and gives clean bakes. 2. Adjust AO Baking Settings in Substance Painter If you must use thick geometry: In the Bake Mesh Maps window, tweak:Max Frontal Distance: Increase it slightly (e.g., from 0.01 to 0.03).Max Rear Distance: Lower it or tweak based on your mesh.Self Occlusion: Try changing from Always to By Mesh Name.Use Cage: Use a custom cage mesh if you have one to better control ray directions. 3. Manually Clean AO Map After baking, you can paint out or soften overly dark AO areas directly in Painter’s 2D view using a paint layer and AO as a mask or fill. 4. Rework Pocket Geometry in MD If the pocket is too flush with the base garment, increase the offset (e.g., pull the pocket out by 1–2 mm more).You can also freeze and simulate with more distance to force a gap. 5. Use Mesh Naming Conventions for Baking Name overlapping parts distinctly (e.g., Body_Shirt, Pocket_Left) and use "Match by Name" baking in Painter. This reduces baking artifacts between intersecting pieces.

Comment 2: Hello, you can usually check if the side of the normals is correct. If it is still failing, you may take it to a photo editor like Photoshop and invert those areas that you believe remain dark, because the program recognized that they are "flipped".
Reply 1: Thanks for the suggestion! I checked, and the normals are correct especially when I export using the Thin option. The dark areas mostly appear only on parts where I added rendering thickness to the fabric in Marvelous Designer, like pockets and layered elements. That seems to be what's causing the issue during the AO bake in Substance Painter.
content_description: This page addresses troubleshooting dark or black Ambient Occlusion bake issues when exporting thick fabric layers from Marvelous Designer to Substance Painter and offers solutions.

title: CLO/MD LiveSync is on Fab — Now with macOS Support!
content:
We are thrilled to announce that [**CLO/MD LiveSync is now available on Fab.com**](https://www.fab.com/listings/e1ecc882-d6c4-4928-b880-5f66d1590bba)! This means you'll be able to download LiveSync and update to newer versions directly through the Epic Games Launcher, without needing to manually place the plugin in the engine folder. **With this update, you can now use CLO/MD LiveSync on macOS as well**! 🚀

You can get it by navigating to the listing and clicking 'Add to My Library' after signing in. Then, you can find it by searching for 'LiveSync' in Library > Fab Library on the Epic Games Launcher. **Please note that this is available for Unreal Engine 5.6 and later versions**.

![7d66e68daab7461cb7e370a02585d8aa](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/c68de71f63fa47bb9464917bc07a9e95/images/7d66e68daab7461cb7e370a02585d8aaUntitled-1.jpg)

![b398547db6eb47a09ac0f246b434e2dc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/c68de71f63fa47bb9464917bc07a9e95/images/b398547db6eb47a09ac0f246b434e2dcimage.png)

We are currently working on supporting the new MetaHuman Parametric Body in both CLO and Marvelous Designer, as well as creating a series of tutorial videos for using CLO/MD LiveSync (check out [**the latest updates for MetaHuman in Unreal Engine 5.6**](https://www.metahuman.com/en-US/news/metahuman-leaves-early-access-with-a-feature-packed-new-release)). In the meantime, please refer to [**the existing documentation for LiveSync 2**](https://connect-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/45247124078873-User-guide-for-LiveSync-2). Stay tuned for more updates! 🙂

Best regards,

Bryan![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/c68de71f63fa47bb9464917bc07a9e95/images/8a95bc78dd2a491891621e1cc855274fCLO_LiveSyncPromo_Still_No_Title_Expand.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi,I’m using CLO Version 2025.1.240, and the “Enable LiveSync” checkbox is turned on.However, I can’t find the “CLO/MD Live Sync Editor” option under Window in Unreal Engine — it simply doesn’t appear.I’ve tried with Unreal Engine versions 5.5.4 and 5.6.1.I also manually placed the LiveSync plugin underC:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.6\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace and UE_5.5\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace,and for UE 5.6, I additionally tried with install from Fab.The plugin shows up as installed and was enabled under “Plugins”, but the option still doesn’t appear under the Window menu.Could someone please help or advise?Best regards,Anastasia

Comment 2: Starting with CLO 2025.0.324 (Individual), a new LiveSync setting has been introduced that allows users to enable or disable the feature. For more details, please refer to the relevant documentation.For CLO Enterprise and Marvelous Designer, version numbers will be announced once the corresponding patch releases are rolled out.
Reply 1: I can't find in the documentation how to export the fur strand to Unreal properly, or to another software. Can you help me out?
Reply 2: Hi Sofia, exporting the Fur Strand fabric type via LiveSync is identical to the export process for Fur (Render Only) fabric type. The steps can be found in the following documentation: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/c68de71f63fa47bb9464917bc07a9e95 there are any issues, please let me know so that my team and I can review and resolve them. 🙂
content_description: This page announces the availability of CLO/MD LiveSync on Fab.com for easy download and updates via the Epic Games Launcher, now supporting macOS and Unreal Engine 5.6+.

title: Stylized Concept Art Meets 3D: How Marvelous Designer Enhances Illustration in Civilization 7
content:
## _Discover how artists like_[ _Ryan Andrade_](https://www.artstation.com/ryanandrade) _use Marvelous Designer to elevate concept art—combining 3D cloth simulation with traditional illustration techniques to create dramatic, painterly visuals for games like Civilization 7. From dynamic character poses to time-saving workflows, Marvelous Designer bridges the gap between realism and stylization in modern game development._

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kK_JrrP9m2U?start=0

# **Interview with**[**Ryan Andrade**](https://www.artstation.com/ryanandrade)**| Civilization 7 | Lead Concept Artist at Firaxis**

# **Can you tell us a bit about yourself and your work on Civilization 7?**

![77b9152e98a4438cad07da520233a33a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/77b9152e98a4438cad07da520233a33aCopy%20of%20FranceLP_Thumbnail.jpg) My concept artwork has always had a heavy emphasis on 3D. I picked up Marvelous Designer back in 2014-ish when I was in college. I started using Marvelous Designer as a reference for painting more believable clothing folds for illustrations, and that’s essentially how I use it now on Civilization.

# **Civilization 7 features a stylized look. What led you to incorporate Marvelous Designer into your workflow, and how did it support the artistic direction?**

![bd2095716f384fda8836991994d459c6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/bd2095716f384fda8836991994d459c6Copy%20of%20XerxesLP_Thumb.jpg) Civ 7’s aesthetic is dark and moody, and our art director had tons of chiaroscuro paintings for us to reference early in production. Baroque and Renaissance era painters are masters of clothing folds (amongst many other things), and so I once again turned to Marvelous Designer to serve as my reference. Those old masters of course hired models to pose for days while they painted, later painters like Norman Rockwell would use photo reference of hired models for the same effect. For my purposes, I see Marvelous Designer as an evolution on that, allowing me to dress and pose characters which then inform my illustrations.

# **Workflow & Tools – Could you walk us through the key tools and software you used throughout the project?**

The first step often happens in Blender where I’m blocking out loose composition ideas with simple geometry. From there I’ll use Daz for more articulated and detailed characters, and put those characters in Marvelous Designer for cloth simulation. Then it’s back to Blender for lights & materials, and lastly is Photoshop for making brushy paint strokes.

# **Can you share some standout moments where Marvelous Designer played a crucial role in creating iconic scenes or characters?**

![c99c92dc2fe448bba83c11e3aaf6251a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/c99c92dc2fe448bba83c11e3aaf6251aCopy%20of%20FranceLP.jpg)_1) final painting_  


The French layer painting for Civ 7 was one of my favorite use cases for Marvelous. The focal point is a woman in a dress hoisting a flag in really dramatic lighting, which would have been hard to paint from scratch without 3D. The great thing about Marvelous is when you’re able to re-use and tweak older assets for new projects, in this case I already made 90% of the stuff I needed, which saved a lot of time.

![c98c161f97374a2083f7e7b5eee0bd87](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/c98c161f97374a2083f7e7b5eee0bd87Copy%20of%20FranceLP_Process.jpg)_2) underpainting made using the 3D as a reference_

![2896955048b4439482a53ee5c208dd8e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/2896955048b4439482a53ee5c208dd8eCopy%20of%20FranceLP_Process2.jpg) _3) raw render from Blender using Marvelous Designer and Daz for the figures_  


The Xerxes illustration was a similar scenario, with tons of robed figures right up in front of the camera. Using Marvelous along with Blender gave me a solid foundation for my painting.

![30eeaee8c31546d7927a31174fba68fc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/30eeaee8c31546d7927a31174fba68fcCopy%20of%20XerxesLP.jpg)_1) Final painting_

![5e8b394b4175451ab9611e17aff0a32f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/0c35626a8bb045d9913382c279c8ce43/images/5e8b394b4175451ab9611e17aff0a32fCopy%20of%20XerxesProcess.jpg) _2) raw render from Blender using Marvelous Designer & Daz for the figures_

# **What advice would you give to artists who want to use Marvelous Designer for concept art?**

Budget your time wisely, at least for professional work. Decide which characters in a scene will benefit most from detailed cloth sim, and which could make do without.

# **How would you describe your experience working with Marvelous Designer on this project?**

Marvelous is my go-to cloth simulation tool, I’ve used it for all sorts of personal and professional projects, and so far no other program comes close to matching its features.

#

content_description: This webpage explores how lead concept artist Ryan Andrade integrates Marvelous Designer’s 3D cloth simulation into his workflow to create dynamic, painterly concept art for Civilization 7, blending realism and stylization to enhance game visuals efficiently.
